original_poem:
ਅੱਜ ਆਖਾਂ ਵਾਰਿਸ ਸ਼ਾਹ ਨੂੰ, ਕਿਤੋਂ ਕਬਰਾਂ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਬੋਲ
ਤੇ ਅੱਜ ਕਿਤਾਬ-ਏ-ਇਸ਼ਕ ਦਾ, ਕੋਈ ਅਗਲਾ ਵਰਕਾ ਫੋਲ

ਇੱਕ ਰੋਈ ਸੀ ਧੀ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ, ਤੂੰ ਲਿਖ ਲਿਖ ਮਾਰੇ ਵੈਨ
ਅੱਜ ਲੱਖਾਂ ਧੀਆਂ ਰੋ ਰਹੀਆਂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਵਾਰਿਸ ਸ਼ਾਹ ਨੂੰ ਕਹਿਨ

ਉਠ ਦਰਦਮੰਦਾਂ ਦੀ ਦਰਦ ਦੀ, ਤੂੰ ਲਿਖ ਲਿਖ ਸਾਹ ਨੰਵੇਂ
ਅੱਜ ਦੇ ਖੂਨ ਰੰਗੇ ਖੇਤਾਂ ਤੋਂ, ਵਾਰਿਸ ਸ਼ਾਹ ਕਈਆਂ ਨਵੇਂ

ਰੋਹਾਂ ਡਿੱਲਾਂ ਪਿਆਰੀਆਂ, ਦੇ ਇਸ਼ਕਾਂ ਸੱਜਣਾਂ ਦੀ
ਅੱਜ ਤਰਸ ਵਿੰਡੀ ਆਂਵਣੀ, ਫਿਰਦੀ ਪਿੰਡਾਂ ਸਜਣਾਂ ਦੀ

ਧਰਤੀ ਤੇ ਕੁਹੜੇ ਵੇਲਾਂ, ਕੁਝ ਭੀ ਦਿਲ ਤੋਂ ਮਿੱਟਦੇ ਨਹੀਂ
ਇਕ ਵਾਰ ਵਾਰਿਸ ਸ਼ਾਹ, ਤੂੰ ਵਾਰਿਸ ਸ਼ਾਹ ਨਹੀਂ ਲਿਖਿਆ ਤਾਂਹੀ!
translated_poem:
Today, I call Waris Shah, speak from your grave
And turn to the next page of the book of love

Once, a daughter of Punjab wept, and you wrote a long saga of pain
Today, a million daughters cry to you, Waris Shah, speak up again

Rise, O compassionate soul, and look at your Punjab
Fields are lined with corpses and blood rains through the sky

The beloveds once adorned by your songs now wander homeless and forlorn
The land of love is barren, and despair looms large in every home

The callousness that has taken root will not be erased so soon
Only you, Waris Shah, can write again the tale of a broken hearted world.

preprocessing.alignment_note: Stanza counts match and alignment confidence is high.

And turn to the next page of the book of love
stanzas.loss_note: ਕਿਤਾਬ-ਏ-ਇਸ਼ਕ is not a generic 'book of love' but a direct invocation of Waris Shah's Heer Ranjha as Punjab's sacred literary monument; ਵਰਕਾ ਫੋਲ (turn a page) carries the specific weight of continuing an unfinished sacred text, lost in translation.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: Heer Ranjha as the unfinished sacred record of Punjab's suffering
summoning the dead poet as the only witness capable of bearing this new grief

source_lines: ਇੱਕ ਰੋਈ ਸੀ ਧੀ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ, ਤੂੰ ਲਿਖ ਲਿਖ ਮਾਰੇ ਵੈਨ

translated_lines: Once, a daughter of Punjab wept, and you wrote a long saga of pain
Today, a million daughters cry to you, Waris Shah, speak up again
stanzas.loss_note: ਵੈਨ is a specific Punjabi women's oral mourning form, not merely a 'saga of pain'; ਧੀ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ refers specifically to Heer, whose singular grief Waris Shah immortalised, and the contrast with ਲੱਖਾਂ ਧੀਆਂ (a million daughters) is the poem's central partition wound.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: Heer as the singular embodiment of Punjab's pre-partition grief
the mass violation of women during the 1947 partition massacres

source_lines: ਉਠ ਦਰਦਮੰਦਾਂ ਦੀ ਦਰਦ ਦੀ, ਤੂੰ ਲਿਖ ਲਿਖ ਸਾਹ ਨੰਵੇਂ

translated_lines: Rise, O compassionate soul, and look at your Punjab
Fields are lined with corpses and blood rains through the sky
stanzas.loss_note: The translation abandons the source almost entirely; ਦਰਦਮੰਦਾਂ ਦੀ ਦਰਦ (the pain of the pain-bearers) is a Sufi devotional register invoking Waris Shah's own compassionate tradition, and ਖੂਨ ਰੰਗੇ ਖੇਤਾਂ (blood-soaked fields) is a concrete partition image rendered abstractly as 'blood rains through the sky'.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: Punjab's agricultural heartland turned into a site of partition massacre

translated_lines: The beloveds once adorned by your songs now wander homeless and forlorn

stanzas.loss_note: ਰੋਹਾਂ ਡਿੱਲਾਂ are specific geographical place-names in Punjab associated with the landscape of Heer Ranjha, not merely abstract 'beloveds adorned by songs'; their loss signals the erasure of a named homeland.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: named Punjabi villages as the now-lost geography of Waris Shah's love epic
desolation wandering through villages like a ghost after partition
